messages:
mariam: Heads up: eu-west GPU pool (eu-west) is dropping hosts — ~35% capacity impacted, p95 token latency up to 1.2s, 503 spikes. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/infra/eu-west
infra-bot: [ALERT] check_failures=82, failing_hosts=14, health_status=DEGRADED :rotating_light:
sahil: I'm oncall but stepping out for ~8m, ping if urgent
leo: I'm online. mariam what's the current traffic split to eu-west?
mariam: current GSLB weights: eu-west 48%, na-east 36%, apac 16%. Need to shift some load. Suggest gradual -15% eu-west -> distribute to na-east +10 apac +5 over 5m intervals.
anya: Prefer gradual to reduce cold-start/kv-warmup. Reminder: prefix/KV cache is per-region; expect a cache-miss spike when we move traffic.
sahil: Could we instead enable degraded-model fallback in eu-west for non-critical routes to avoid cross-region egress? That might keep latency but reduce capacity needs.
mariam: we have fallback enabled for a subset of high-tier customers, not global. Rolling that global is riskier than steering for now.
leo: Ok I'll prepare the GSLB weight change. Command (runbook):
```
redwood-gslb update-weights --policy global --changes "eu-west:-15,na-east:+10,apac:+5" --gradual 5m
```
netops: note — there's a partial egress NAT issue in eu-west causing some long-lived TCP resets; lowering DNS TTL can help failover faster (recommend TTL=10s temporarily).
anya: Proposed plan: 1) Apply -15% eu-west immediately, spread to na-east/apac as above. 2) Pre-warm pools in na-east and watch autoscaler. 3) Monitor KV cache hit rate + p95 + 503 rate. 4) If errors >0.5% escalate to full soft-evac.
mariam: applying weight update now
mariam: DONE — ran `redwood-gslb update-weights --policy global --changes "eu-west:-15,na-east:+10,apac:+5" --gradual 5m` (no blocking errors)
infra-bot: GSLB weights updated: eu-west=33%, na-east=46%, apac=21% (change_id=chg-7821)
sahil: seeing request spike in na-east, autoscaler triggered but instance cold-starts ~90s. getting a short blip of 503s, watching.
leo: cost note — expected capacity/egress cost delta ~+22% over baseline if traffic remains shifted; tag billing with incident-id IN-2026-042
anya: keep an eye on KV cache warming. If we can keep p95 < 800ms we can stop draining and start reversing the change sooner.
mariam: infra team investigating host driver restarts as root cause on some nodes. If recovery >45m propose soft-evac: set eu-west=0% for non-enterprise customers and perform graceful drain for enterprise customers.
oncall-bot: runbook acknowledged — https://runbooks.redwood/evacuation-guide
leo: I'll coordinate a pre-warm job for heavy models in na-east to minimize further 503s
anya: will notify customers if this goes beyond 30m via #customer-alerts
sahil: +1, I'll prepare a quick cost/impact note for finance
mariam: thanks all. ping here with any new anomalies. :thumbsup:
leo: :thumbsup:
anya: :thumbsup:
netops: monitoring network path; will post updates
infra-bot: incident tag IN-2026-042 attached, timeline started
